# Deckard 1.13.0 - an installer

Deckard can now be installed with a Setup program, as well as unzipped.

## What is new

- **An installer.** Each release now has `Deckard-Setup-<version>.exe` next to the zip. Run it and Deckard is installed for you alone, with no administrator rights, into `%LocalAppData%\Programs\Deckard`, with an entry in the Start menu and one in Windows' Installed apps for uninstalling. The installer holds the same files as the zip (the window, `Deckard.Cli.exe`, the guides and the Claude skill) and is smaller to download.
- **Updating is running the newer Setup.** Download the newer `Deckard-Setup-<version>.exe` from the release page and run it: it replaces the installed copy, including removing any file the new version no longer has. Your settings, saved profiles and baselines are not touched, because they are not stored in the install folder.

## Things to know

- **Windows will warn the first time.** The installer is not signed, so Windows SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your PC" when you run it: choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. This is the same warning the zip's `Deckard.exe` gives.
- **Close Deckard before you update.** Setup can close a running Deckard so its files can be replaced, but anything unsaved in the window would be lost.
- **The install folder is fixed.** There is no folder page, because an update clears the folder before copying and so it must hold nothing but Deckard.
- **Updates are still not automatic.** The "update available" banner still opens the release page; you download and run the Setup yourself.
- **The zip is still published**, and an unzipped copy is separate from an installed one: the installer does not look for, or replace, a copy you unzipped somewhere.
